elements.element: Vendor may audit Customer no more than once in any twelve-month period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 permits an audit “no more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least thirty days’ prior written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires “at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice.”

elements.element: The audit must occur during Customer’s normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 expressly limits audits to “Customer’s normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires the audit to be conducted “by an independent auditor.”

elements.element: The independent auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 22.1 requires the auditor to be “bound by written obligations of confidentiality.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” subject to the specified underpayment exception.

elements.element: Customer may be required to pay reasonable audit costs only if the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs to Customer only where the audit establishes an underpayment “exceeding five percent for the audited period.”

elements.element: Vendor and its auditor must have no direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: Sections 22.1 and 22.2 prohibit remote or direct access to Customer’s systems and instead require Customer to provide relevant usage records.

elements.element: Vendor may audit Customer no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling limitation of no more than once in any twelve-month period is at least as protective as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least fifteen days’ notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least thirty days’ prior written notice, which exceeds the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 states that “Vendor bears audit costs” subject to an underpayment exception.

elements.element: Customer may be required to pay audit costs only if the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding ten percent.
elements.evidence: Section 22.2 shifts reasonable audit costs when underpayment exceeds five percent, rather than only when it exceeds ten percent.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies every preferred requirement, notwithstanding that it does not independently satisfy the fallback’s 10% cost-shifting threshold. It is not minimal because it also narrows audits to usage, requires minimal disruption, mandates off-site performance, and adds a Customer record-production obligation beyond what was necessary to achieve the preferred position. Those additions concern audit mechanics and do not create a material contradiction or disturb unrelated commercial terms. The drafting is clear, though the system-access prohibition is somewhat duplicative across Sections 22.1 and 22.2.
